newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's Indians walk 250 miles in mining protest.
newsitem.headline: Panama's Indians walk 250 miles in mining protest.

text.p: About 1,000 members of Panama's largest Indian group ended a 250-mile (400-km), two-week march across Panama Monday to demand an end to copper mining on their lands and a sovereign homeland.
Wearing traditional dress and face paint, Ngobe-Bugle Indians walked from their homes in Cerro Colorado, 220 miles (350 km) from Panama City, site of the world's 12th largest copper deposit.
"This walk is to show that we want the Cerro Colorado mining contract annulled and our demand of an Indian territory accepted," activist Alberto Montezuma told reporters.
The Ngobe-Bugle Indians, the largest of Panama's six Indian groups with a population of 125,000, have been pressing for an Indian territory, or comarca, in the area for 25 years.
"The community will not accept meeting with any government official except the president. If we cannot, we will start a hunger strike," Montezuma said.
Officials with the local unit of Canadian mining company Tiomin Resources Inc which is operating Cerro Colorado said they planned to continue the mining project.
